neighbours.label: The English pronoun tokens 'they' and 'them' when referring back to people or things.
fire: The volunteers finished early, so we thanked them before closing the hall.
Several packages arrived today, and they are waiting near the reception desk.
The seedlings need shelter because they cannot tolerate a hard frost.
Two musicians missed the train, but a friend offered to collect them.
The spare keys were missing until the caretaker found them beneath a newspaper.
The hikers checked the map before they followed the path into the valley.
The instructions were confusing, so I read them a second time.
The committee members agreed that they would meet again after the holiday.
quiet: One volunteer stayed late, so we thanked him before locking the hall.
A package arrived this morning and remains beside the reception desk.
The gardener protected each seedling from the cold with a small cover.
A musician missed the bus, and a friend offered him a lift home.
The caretaker searched beneath the newspaper and recovered a spare key.
A hiker checked the map carefully before following the path into the valley.
Because the instructions were confusing, I read the entire page again.
The committee chair agreed that he would arrange another meeting after the holiday.

notes: The opposite pole favors masculine singular pronouns. Exploratory readings also found it firing, so the registered token set is deliberately a possible partial trigger, not a claim to cover every non-masculine pronoun.
